paras: The threatened lynching of George Hadington took place at Savannah, Tennessee, in late June 1881, after Hadington, a Black man, was arrested on a charge of attempting to assault a fourteen-year-old white girl. The only report found, a brief in the Memphis Daily Appeal, said that the arrest caused "considerable excitement" and that threats to lynch him had been made, but it reported no attack.

Hadington was accused of attempting to "outrage" Mary Sanderson, whom the paper described as "a little white girl" aged fourteen. According to the brief, she was "severely bruised" and her assailant fled when she screamed for help.

Hadington was arrested at Savannah on the charge on a Wednesday, which, counting back from the paper's Sunday, July 3 issue, was June 29. Excitement followed the arrest, and threats were made to lynch him, though the item does not say who made them or whether a crowd gathered.
No report of a trial, a further move against Hadington, or his fate appears in the coverage.

The case appeared as one short paragraph under the Tennessee heading of the Memphis Daily Appeal's "News from Our Neighbors" column, as the last of several local items that included a new synagogue, childhood illnesses and a farmer's rye crop. The paper presented the accusation as a "charge" but then called Hadington "the black fiend" and "the villain" and reported the lynching threats without comment. The item named no county; it is placed in Tennessee only by the heading under which it ran.

reader.title: Threatened lynching of George Hadington
bases: The only report says that after Hadington's arrest 'threats to lynch the villain have been made' amid 'considerable excitement'; no crowd action is reported (A1).
A1 reports only threats to lynch a man held on an attempted-outrage charge; no killing, no attack and no crowd of any size are reported, so this is a threatened lynching at most.
One brief in the Memphis Daily Appeal (A1) is the only report found; no other paper, follow-up or court report appears.

quotes: At Savannah last Wednesday a negro, George Hadington, was arrested on a charge of attempting to outrage a little white girl, Mary Sanderson, aged fourteen years.
She was severely bruised by the black fiend, who was frightened away by her screams for assistance.
Considerable excitement exists, and threats to lynch the villain have been made.
